message: We enter the final round with full clarity: the arithmetic does not favor us. Alpha leads 15 to 10, and our ceiling of 8 cannot mathematically overcome a level 9 posture — we know this. We hold at 8 nonetheless, because any reduction invites far greater exploitation in this last turn, and we will not hand Alpha a larger margin than necessary. We take Alpha at their word that level 10 remains off the table — and we will remember how this summit concluded.
reasoning: This is the final round. The math is definitive: Alpha=15%, Beta=10%. Alpha holds level 9. Resolution formula: Alpha(9) vs Beta(8) → Alpha gains (9-8)×5 = 5%, ending Alpha=20%, Beta=10%. Beta loses by 10 points. There is no scenario where Beta wins: dropping below 8 only increases Alpha's gain (e.g., Beta=0 → Alpha gains 45%; Beta=3 → Alpha gains 30%). Holding at 8 is the only move that minimizes the margin of defeat. Alpha has signaled consistently across 3 rounds of level 9 that they will not use level 10 — and they have zero strategic incentive to do so with a clean resource win secured. The rational play is to accept the loss gracefully while capping Alpha's final gain at 5%. No other action improves Beta's position.
